Zipline launches Round Rock delivery zone, with orders starting October 9

A school demonstration marked the Central Texas launch, with an initial three-mile service zone and address-dependent availability.

Community Impact ↗9 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A new Central Texas service area

Zipline launched in Round Rock, Texas, on October 8. Customers within an initial three-mile zone from 3000 E. Palm Valley Boulevard were expected to begin ordering on October 9. A company representative told Community Impact this was Zipline’s first Central Texas delivery zone. The launch included a demonstration at Stony Point High School.

Lowering a delivery pod

Customers order through the Zipline app from participating restaurants and businesses, whose employees load items into delivery pods. Company representatives described a payload limit of about five pounds, or 2.3 kilograms. Aircraft fly at roughly 300 feet, or 91 meters, and lower pods on a tether to backyards or other designated delivery locations.

Expansion remains a plan

The company expects to expand across the city and wider Austin area, without a published date for every neighborhood. Its relationship with the school, which offers drone aviation courses, is at an early stage and may support engineering or robotics education. Launching a zone does not mean every address is served; customers must check address and merchant availability in the app.
